sections.title: Basic Concept of Synonyms and Antonyms
sections.content: Synonyms are words that have the same or nearly the same meaning. Antonyms are words that have opposite meanings. In competitive examinations, you are usually asked to identify the correct synonym or antonym of a given word.

sections.title: Direct Synonym Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the basic meaning of the given word. Step 2: Compare the meanings of the options. Step 3: The option that gives the closest meaning is the correct synonym. Example: Happy → Joyful.

sections.title: Direct Antonym Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the exact meaning of the given word. Step 2: Look for a word with the opposite meaning. Step 3: The option that gives the completely opposite meaning is the correct antonym. Example: Hot → Cold.

sections.title: Odd Word Out (Synonym Group)
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meanings of all the words. Step 2: Identify the word whose meaning is different from the others. Step 3: That word will be the odd one out. Example: Happy, Joyful, Cheerful, Angry → Angry is the odd word.

sections.title: Word Meaning Strategy
sections.content: Identifying prefixes, roots, or common usage of a word helps in understanding its meaning. The meaning can also be guessed based on context.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Assuming meaning only by looking at spelling. 2. Considering similar-looking words as having the same meaning. 3. Choosing meaning without considering context.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: A synonym gives a similar meaning while an antonym gives the opposite meaning. The correct answer is chosen by comparing the meanings of the options. In odd word out questions, identifying the meaning group is important.

tricks.title: Meaning First Rule
tricks.explanation: First recall the general meaning of the word.

tricks.title: Opposite Thinking Trick
tricks.explanation: While finding an antonym, think about the opposite meaning of the word.

tricks.title: Group Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: In odd word questions, first group the words with similar meanings.
tricks.example: Big, Large, Huge, Tiny → Tiny is different.

tricks.title: Common Usage Trick
tricks.explanation: Recognize words that are commonly used with similar meanings in everyday language.
tricks.example: Begin and Start have similar meanings.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Removing incorrect options helps in finding the correct answer quickly.
tricks.example: If two words clearly have opposite meanings, one may be the antonym.

tricks.title: Context Guessing Trick
tricks.explanation: If you do not fully remember the meaning, guess it based on usage in context.

tricks.title: Prefix Clue Trick
tricks.explanation: Some prefixes provide clues to the meaning of the word.

tricks.title: Opposite Pair Memory
tricks.explanation: Some words are commonly remembered in opposite pairs.
